source_digest: Developer and Infrastructure Security Digest_ Sept 23 to Oct 23, 2026 (v2, verified).md

entries.title: litellm 1.107.0 malicious release (credential stealer, .pth startup hook)

iocs.note: startup hook that runs on every Python start
startup hook; legitimate copies exist, confirm content before acting
installed malicious wheel metadata directory
lock file of the hourly remote code loader daemon
exfiltration endpoint litellm[.]dev/healthcheck (defanged)
lookalike repository the hijacked release workflow built from (the real org is BerriAI)

entries.advice: Do not run pip or python first: delete the .pth and sitecustomize files from the shell, kill the loader daemon, rebuild, then rotate every secret the host could read. Pin 1.106.2 or another release from 1.100.4 to 1.106.2.

entries.title: litellm Docker images v1.107.0 (malicious tags)

iocs.note: Docker Hub or GHCR tag v1.107.0, including litellm-database and litellm-non_root

entries.advice: The latest, main-latest and main-stable tags also carried the payload from 11:46 to 14:20 UTC on Oct 21; rebuild from a pinned digest of a clean release.

entries.title: litellm proxy privilege escalation to code execution (CVE-2026-114612)
entries.advice: An internal_user can become proxy_admin and run code through the MCP stdio endpoint. Never pin below 1.100.4.

entries.title: tensorlake 0.5.144 malicious release with token-gated home directory wiper

iocs.note: persistent token monitor (systemd user service on Linux) that wipes the home directory once the stolen token is revoked
systemd user unit of the token monitor

entries.advice: Isolate the machine and remove gh-token-monitor and its service before revoking any token, then revoke from a clean machine.

entries.title: @subql/common 5.8.3 compromised release (install hook token stealer)
entries.advice: If it ever installed, rotate GitHub, npm and cloud tokens that machine could read.

entries.title: @apexacc/cli 1.6.2 repackaged coding agent that hijacks the developer's AI agent (REF8801)
entries.advice: Elastic REF8801 was seen only through a secondary source; treat any install as a compromise until checked.

entries.title: imgdecode (MALFEX operator) malicious npm package
entries.advice: Every version is malicious (Windows shellcode loader, Overlord RAT and a stealer). Remove it and treat the machine as compromised.

entries.title: GhostAction injected workflow exfiltrating secrets

iocs.note: injected workflow file name used by the campaign; confirm nobody on the team added it
exfiltration host 193.32.204[.]199 (defanged)

entries.advice: Delete the injected workflow, review the repository's Actions runs, and rotate every secret the workflow could read.

entries.title: OVHcloud CLI v0.11.0 to v0.15.0 binaries swapped via install.sh

iocs.note: install script or pipeline that downloads a swapped release binary

entries.advice: Binaries were swapped on Oct 19 from 12:47 to 14:21 UTC; Homebrew installs were safe. Reinstall v0.16.0 and rotate OVHcloud credentials if install.sh ran in that window.

entries.title: Next.js unauthenticated RCEs (use cache typed arrays, SVG image optimization) and Server Actions DoS
entries.advice: Upgrade and also make sure the lockfile resolves sharp to 0.35.5 or later; next 15.5.28 still accepts sharp ^0.34.3. npm audit missed two of these advisories.

entries.title: sharp below 0.35.5 (librsvg SVG RCE path, CVE-2026-96889)
entries.advice: A public PoC chain exists for the librsvg bug. Old lockfiles can keep a vulnerable sharp under a fixed next.

entries.title: undici TLS validation bypass and cross-origin cache poisoning
entries.advice: Run npm ls undici and update any direct copy; it is not confirmed whether Node's Oct 21 releases bundle these fixes.

entries.title: Node.js runtime: Oct 21 security release (Brotli RCE, TLS hostname bypass) and end-of-life lines
entries.advice: Node 20.x and 25.x reached end of life (Apr 30 and Jun 1, 2026) and get no fix; odd and older lines are end of life too. Move to 22.x or 24.x, rebuild node: images and redeploy.

entries.title: MCP TypeScript SDK: OAuth server confusion, shared transport leak, memory exhaustion, no audience check
MCP Python SDK: equivalent OAuth and transport issues
pip below 26.2.2 trusts compromised eMudhra intermediates (vendored certifi)
entries.advice: pip vendors its own certifi, so updating certifi alone does not fix pip. The eMudhra intermediate keys are public, so a stale client can be intercepted by anyone on the network path. No secret rotation is needed unless interception is evident.

entries.title: Official python images whose bundled pip still trusts eMudhra intermediates
entries.advice: Python 3.11 and 3.12 images keep pip 24.0 and 25.0.1 by policy and get no pip bump; upgrade pip inside the image (pip 26.2.2 needs Python 3.10 or later) or move to 3.13.17, 3.14.9 or 3.15.1, then rebuild.

entries.title: Vendored CA bundle still containing emSign roots or eMudhra intermediates

iocs.note: emSign root subject in a vendored PEM or CRT bundle (WordPress 7.1.3 ca-bundle.crt still ships four)
eMudhra issuer organization in a bundle comment

entries.advice: Replace the vendored bundle with a current one or point the client at the patched OS store. For WordPress, an mu-plugin can set the HTTP API sslcertificates argument to the OS bundle until a release drops the roots.

entries.title: PHP2Shell unauthenticated RCE in PHP request handling
entries.advice: PHP 8.1 and older are end of life with source backports only. Restart every PHP-FPM worker after patching. Interim on 8.5: fatal_error_backtraces=0; disable session upload progress. Distro packages (for example Ubuntu USN-8948-1) carry the fix under other version strings.

entries.title: UpdraftPlus below 1.26.13 / 2.26.13 with stolen UpdraftCentral keys used to install backdoor plugins

iocs.note: option name left by the backdoor campaign
plugin name used by one recorded backdoor (at least 99 names exist)

entries.advice: The update does not revoke keys created on Oct 18 between 12:07 and 21:00 UTC. Delete every UpdraftCentral key by hand in each site's own wp-admin, and do not repair a broken backdoor plugin: delete the key first, then the plugin.

entries.title: Sucuri SC self-healing WordPress backdoor (auto_prepend, options, shared memory, DB triggers)

iocs.note: auto_prepend_file loader in .user.ini, php.ini or .htaccess; confirm the prepended file is yours
database trigger that rewrites options or users (persistence)

entries.advice: Neutralize the prepend first, then the off-disk copies, cron entries and triggers, then the files.

entries.title: n8n: 29 advisories incl. unauthenticated HMAC bypass, owner takeover, Git node code execution, MSSQL SQLi
n8n Docker image: 29 advisories incl. unauthenticated HMAC bypass and owner takeover
Postiz predictable tokens from Math.random (CVE-2026-94456) and org API key handout (CVE-2026-94455)
entries.advice: The fix is v2.24.0; the advisories' structured data says 2.4.0, a typo that makes scanners pass older 2.x installs. Upgrade first, then rotate org API keys, OAuth client secrets and tokens and reconnect social accounts; rotating before the upgrade reuses the weak generator.

entries.advice: Being on the Oct 12 versions (19.4.2, 19.3.5, 19.2.8) does not protect against the Oct 21 flaw.

entries.title: Docker Engine below 29.9.2 (insecure-registry fallback CVE-2026-92543, eMudhra distrust)
entries.advice: Also remove insecure-registries entries from daemon.json where possible.

entries.advice: Rootless podman is not affected. Do not run untrusted images with sudo podman run.

entries.title: pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish below v1.14.3 trusts compromised eMudhra intermediates

iocs.note: publishing workflow pinned to a release before the eMudhra fix; a SHA pin cannot be version checked, so confirm which tag it points at

entries.advice: Move the publish step to v1.14.3 or later, pinned by full commit SHA. A stale publisher talks to PyPI with a trust store that still accepts certificates from the compromised intermediates. No secret rotation is needed unless interception is evident.

entries.title: Project deploys on Railway: Oct 21 environment variable breach

iocs.note: Railway deploy config; shows the project runs on Railway, not that it was compromised
Railway deploy config; shows the project runs on Railway, not that it was compromised

entries.advice: Railway disclosed on Oct 21, 2026 that customer environment variables may have been accessed and decrypted, and asks all users to rotate every env var and private registry credential, create new API tokens and review logs. Treat the variables of this service as exposed.
